change_summary: Generated/third-party Rust execution fails closed before local rustc and names SciRust-Hub/RemoteOps as the required external OS-isolated boundary.
Local rustc and local Wasmtime execution are explicitly named trusted-only escape hatches.
Rust source and WASM module byte budgets are enforced before compilation/JIT allocation paths.
Wasmtime StoreLimits bound linear memory, table elements, instances, memories and tables for the local trusted diagnostic path.
Trusted local rustc uses a separate compile timeout, drains stderr concurrently, retains a bounded diagnostic prefix and bounds the produced module before reading it.
Security and scientific documentation stop describing in-process Wasmtime as a hostile-code OS sandbox.

discarded_attempts.reason: Three test callsites retained the pre-rename execute method. They were updated to execute_trusted_wasm; no security limit or gate was weakened.

acceptance_met: Untrusted Rust no longer launches local rustc through the public PAPERS path.
Source/module bytes, Wasmtime Store memory/table/instance counts, compile timeout and compiler diagnostics are bounded on the local trusted diagnostic path.
The exact integrated tree equals the candidate tree that passed the full repository CI.
acceptance_pending: Wire generated Rust/WASM JIT execution to a concretely qualified SciRust-Hub/RemoteOps backend with stronger-than-process OS isolation, default-deny network and enforceable resource budgets.
Retain evidence that the selected backend actually enforces the requested isolation/resource/network policy; a declarative TaskSpec or detected sandbox binary alone is insufficient.
The local StoreLimits are not evidence that all Wasmtime engine/JIT memory is globally bounded.

batch.note: This PR completes the 50-PR remediation batch but does not close PAPERS-01.
